ROW 1 — Overview & Filtering
Dashboard · Lists · Custom Rules · Policies · Clients · Rule Tester

Sketch: layout and interaction only. Every panel maps to a route in capability-matrix.md — nothing is drawn without an endpoint behind it. Figures are the real box where they exist: 752,585 rules, 89.7 % hit, 1,108/50,000 entries.

Custom Rules is a validated document, not a CRUD table.

/rules/user takes lines in and gives lines out — there is no per-rule identity, so no per-rule delete or toggle is offered. Save is all-or-nothing.

Policies replaces Pi-hole's Groups.

A policy is a list subset plus an optional schedule, and one address carries at most one assignment — no many-to-many matrix to render. Assignment is edited inline on Clients.

ROW 2 — Runtime & System
Cache · Performance · Upstreams · Settings · Health · Memory · Live Feed

The Runtime three have no Pi-hole equivalent at all: cache lifetime stages and both bounds, per-stage latency percentiles, endpoint health under the adaptive strategy. Same visual language, FAH's own subject matter.

Health and state, never a share-of-traffic pie.

Per-query upstream attribution is deliberately not carried, so the only honest chart is how each endpoint is behaving. `degraded` is explained in place rather than alarmed.
Settings is grouped by config section, not Pi-hole's subsystem tabs — FAH's real axis is mutability. Every field is tagged LIVE or RESTART.

Peak is NOT a slice of the donut — it is a lifetime high-water mark, not part of current RSS. It gets the budget rail instead.

Budgets are drawn as markers, never as walls: nothing enforces memory at runtime, the container runs memory-high=unlimited.

ROW 3 — Phone, 390 × 844
Navigation drawer · Dashboard · Live Feed · Clients

These are the source of truth for the mobile acceptance criteria in p5-04, p5-05 and p5-07 — not a smaller copy of the desktop layout.

Rules they settle: 44 px minimum touch targets; the body never scrolls sideways; the sidebar becomes an overlay drawer below 768 px; table-heavy views become one card per row, never a horizontal table; the Live Feed holds a smaller ring and stops rendering while the page is hidden.

The frames are drawn taller than 844 so the whole page is visible. The Dashboard artboard marks where the fold actually falls.

Nine columns do not survive a phone. One card per event instead: verdict, pipeline and time on the first line, the domain given room to wrap, everything else as metadata.

Ring is 200 here against 500 on desktop, and rendering pauses when the page is hidden — no battery spent drawing rows nobody is watching, and no history to backfill from anyway.

The page most likely to be opened from a phone, usually to answer one question: why is that device blocked.

So the policy chip is on the card, the solid-versus-dashed distinction survives, and rename plus change-policy are the only actions — both one round trip.

Drawn in p5-06, which is also where it was built.

One card per list, never a horizontal table — the rule the other phone frames already establish. A failed, rejected or degraded card grows an explanation block between the header and the partition, and a rejected card replaces Refresh with Delete and re-add: the content gate refuses a body against the cached copy, so neither a refresh nor a disable/enable can clear it.
